correctness.rationale: A geometric fixed point is an orbit-barycentric simplex. Complementary d-independent-set eligibility gives exactly a disjunction of orbit-weight threshold inequalities. Alexander dual of the join gives a union of contractible cones with intersection a join, yielding the homotopy suspension formula. The threshold complex has a contractible least-weight-vertex star; every exterior simplex is a maximal face attached along its entire boundary, proving a wedge of spheres and integral torsion-freeness. The resulting polynomial degree shift is verified algebraically and by 2,474 exhaustive bipartite profiles, one mixed-degree example, and 80 seeded multi-part profiles using direct mod-two chain ranks; computations are finite checks only.

value.rationale: Arbitrary subgroup orbit-size profiles determine all integral Betti dimensions from finite subset-sum calculations, without constructing the potentially enormous ambient simplicial complex. The K_9,4 example has nonzero reduced integral homology in two distinct degrees (2 and 3) while the ambient cut complex has one-degree homology in degree 5. A general structural classification and motivated mixed-dimensional phenomenon go beyond a trivial renaming, a single finite table or the already-known ambient rank.
